21418-the-eugenic-marriage-volume-4-of-4:
Volume four of W. Grant Hague's The Eugenic Marriage, issued in 1913, closes his guide to better living and better babies. Hague was a New York doctor trained at Columbia's College of Physicians and Surgeons. He wrote in the name of eugenics, then a much-praised new science.

The pages give rules for the care of young children in the home. Hague warns against letting babies crawl on cold floors, where draughts run low. Beds, sofas, or raised boards are urged for play instead. Modern readers will read the book as a record of its age, since eugenics is now rejected and condemned.
